name: Back to top
summary: A round link in the end corner that appears once the page has scrolled and takes the reader back to the top.
description:
Use it on long pages: docs, articles, long lists. Put id="top" on an element at the top of the page (the header or the first section) and link to it.

It is a plain same-page link, so it works without JS and moves focus to the top as well as the scroll position. Where scroll-driven animations are supported it stays hidden until the page has scrolled about one screen; elsewhere it is always shown.

classes.name: v-back-to-top
classes.description: The link, fixed in the end corner (bottom right, bottom left in right-to-left). Holds an icon and needs an aria-label.

classes.name: v-back-to-top-progress
classes.description: A ring around the button that fills as the page is read. Add data-v-scroll-progress for browsers without scroll timelines.

states.description: Points at an element at the top of the page. Any id works.

keyboard.action: Follows the link: scrolls to the top and moves focus there.

a11y: While hidden it is visibility: hidden, not just transparent, so it is not a Tab stop and screen readers skip it.
Give it an aria-label such as "Back to top": it shows only an arrow.
Following it moves focus to the target, so keyboard users continue from the top too, not only the viewport.
Smooth scrolling comes from the page and is switched off under reduced motion.

examples.title: Back to top link
examples.description: In this preview it is always in the corner; on a real page it appears after the first screen. Set --v-back-to-top-after to change when, and --v-back-to-top-offset to move it clear of a bottom bar.

hooks.name: data-v-scroll-progress
hooks.description: Fills the progress ring from a scroll listener where scroll timelines are missing.
